newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma votes to keep 51 pct UES for state.
newsitem.headline: Duma votes to keep 51 pct UES for state.

text.p: The Russian State Duma lower house of parliament voted on Friday to keep 51 percent of national national power company Unified Energy System (UES) in state hands, and to limit foreign ownership to 25 percent.
The house approved the bill in a third and final reading -- it still must pass the Federation Council upper chamber of parliament and then be signed into law by President Boris Yeltsin.
The state currently owns a little over 52 percent of the company, UES officials said last month.
Under the UES charter, shareholders must receive permission from the company's directorate in order to vote more than one percent of company shares, regardless of the size of the stake they hold.

The government previously has announced plans to sell this year one percent of UES, as well as 49 percent of telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, 50 percent of insurer Rosgosstrakh and stakes in several oil companies.
Last year Russia sold an 8.49 percent stake in the company.
UES owns the national power grid, has controlling stakes in most regional power utilities and has stakes in a number of generating plants.
The government is mulling reforming the energy structure, and newly appointed Fuirst Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has said prices must go down in the sector.
At 0755 GMT, shares in RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) had fallen to $0.1850 from $0.1910 on the Russian Trading System.
